doc.title: Tyner McCoy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The Meeting and a website discography error
summary: Brown discusses the live album The Meeting with Sonship and points out a wrong date on Tyner's website.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Another album recorded live, again Orrin really mining what he knew was a strength.
Yeah, Orrin was a musicians’ producer, he knew musicians and their music.

So this one recorded in San Francisco at the Great American Music Hall entitled The Meeting and this one-there we go another one of those great drummers Sonship. Woody Theus on drums who recently passed.
He was a good . . . he did pass?
A year or two ago because I know James Newton was working with him and he sent me a message.
Because Charles Fambrough earlier this year, yeah and Wilby, but I didn’t know Sonship had.

And this one you had George Adams, Joe Ford, Charles Fambrough, and Sonship. Now I bring this one up not only because it was a great album and very influential for me, but when I review your discography this one is unfortunately not listed. Well it’s in there but it’s listed as 1963 so was there another album that was recorded called “The Meeting,” or “The Greeting?” That was just on your website.

That’s on your website, so I’m just bringing that up so that whoever is your web master might want to change that because they got this album cover and they have it listed as released in 1963 so I just want to make sure that that’s something I bring to your attention.
Yeah I wonder who would do that.
Because it’s definitely not from ’63, and it’s listed as a trio date.
No, but that’s just one of those things that’s just a technical issue.
Thank’s for bringing that up, it’s good to have it corrected.
